lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: interpreting conditional probability in context

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: In a group of 43, 21 do activity A, 21 do activity B, and 10 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 2/8 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A survey table records: group X with 18 successes and 11 failures; group Y with 8 successes and 13 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 6/10, P(B) = 9/10, and P(A and B) = 54/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.

items.prompt: In a group of 31, 13 do activity A, 11 do activity B, and 7 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 6/10 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 16 successes and 14 failures; group Y with 41 successes and 50 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 3/10, P(B) = 1/10, and P(A and B) = 3/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: In a group of 52, 22 do activity A, 22 do activity B, and 17 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
